title: Sandigan grants exclusion of Romualdez co-accused
summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has allowed the exclusion of a co-accused of former House speaker Martin Romualdez from a P7.4-billion plunder case involving alleged kickbacks from government…

blocks.text: November 29, 2026 | 12:00am
Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has allowed the exclusion of a co-accused of former House speaker Martin Romualdez from a P7.4-billion plunder case involving alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.

In an 11-page resolution, the anti-graft court has granted the prosecution’s request to file an amended information dropping Felicito Cristobal Guevarra from the list of accused as it found that prosecutors satisfied the requirements of a pre-plea exclusion of an accused.
Guevarra is the president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp., a firm allegedly used to funnel the alleged kickbacks for Romualdez.

Under Section 14, Rule 110 of the Revised Rules of Criminal Procedure, a complaint or information may be amended to exclude an accused before he or she enters his or her plea, upon motion by the prosecutors, with notice to the offended party and with leave of court.
The Sandiganbayan said the said rule is applicable in the case since the amendment is being made before Guevarra can enter his plea.

It also agreed with the prosecution that the amendment sought is merely formal in nature and does not prejudice any right of Romualdez, and “do not touch upon the recital of facts constituting the offense charged nor change the theory of the prosecution.”

The anti-graft court also allowed the prosecution to present Guevarra as a witness in the hearings on Romualdez’s petition for bail, in lieu of former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan.

It ruled that Guevarra’s willingness to testify constituted a supervening event that justified the substitution as it conserved the materiality of his testimony in the case, considering that he was allegedly part of the chain in the supposed kickback scheme.
The Office of the Ombudsman is seeking to make Guevarra as a state witness after he returned P343 million in alleged proceeds in connection with the plunder case.

The Sandiganbayan likewise granted the prosecution’s request to keep Guevarra detained at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) while waiting admission to the witness protection program, recognizing that threats to his life and personal security, while not substantiated, are possible.
Guevarra’s arraignment was originally set for Dec. 4, coinciding with the last day of hearings on Romualdez’s bail petition.
Guevarra surrendered to the NBI on Nov. 19 after state prosecutors moved to cancel his passport. He is currently at the agency’s detention facility.
Meanwhile, the Sandiganbayan Third Division has also ordered an investigation on an individual allegedly impersonating a justice to solicit money from a witness in the case against Romualdez.

In an order, the anti-graft court directed the NBI to investigate and determine the identity of the individuals involved, establish the circumstances surrounding the reported solicitation and submit a report to the court.

The information stemmed from an urgent manifestation filed by the Office of the Ombudsman concerning an individual who misrepresented himself in a telephone conversation as the Third Division chairman Associate Justice Karl Miranda.
The person supposedly solicited P300,000 from Guevarra’s son, in connection with the proceedings before this court.
Based on the transcript of a video recording of the phone call, the money would be for the dismissal of the plunder case of Romualdez, wherein Guevarra was originally a co-accused.

The anti-graft court said the incident is a very serious matter and a grave concern, saying the misrepresentation is an “affront” to the justice concerned as well as to the integrity, independence, and authority of the court and the judiciary.
